headline: ASK demands impartial probe into journalist's killing in Netrokona
summary: Human rights organization Ain and Salish Kendra (ASK) has called for an immediate investigation into the shooting death of Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir.
details: Human rights organization Ain and Salish Kendra (ASK) has expressed deep concern and strong condemnation over the killing of journalist Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir in Netrokona's Durgapur.
caption:
A journalist was shot dead in Netrokona, and human rights advocates are now demanding justice. This is a dangerous signal for free press.

Human rights organization Ain and Salish Kendra (ASK) has expressed deep concern and strong condemnation over the killing of journalist Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir in Netrokona's Durgapur.

#Bangladesh #Journalism #PressFreedom #JusticeForAlif #Netrokona #HumanRights

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star

headline_marked: FB posts incite [[mob killing of young man]] in Satkhira
headline: FB posts incite mob killing of young man in Satkhira
summary: Wahiduzzaman Shamim, a madrasa and university graduate who wrote a religious book, was beaten to death after Facebook posts accused him of insulting Islam.
details: Wahiduzzaman Shamim was beaten to death by a mob in Satkhira's Debhata after being accused of making derogatory remarks about Islam. The violence escalated following viral Facebook posts and live broadcasts that identified him and incited a crowd.

An audio recording of a private conversation between Shamim and his wife, recorded during an argument, went viral on October 12. This recording sparked tension and led to allegations that he had insulted religion.

On October 13, a local religious speaker, Fazlul Haque Ameni, went live on Facebook twice, naming Shamim and demanding his punishment. This was followed by a procession of over 200 people who dragged Shamim out of a health complex and beat him again.
Despite attempts by police and medical staff to stop the attackers, Shamim died before reaching Satkhira Medical College Hospital. He leaves behind two children, aged eight years and seven months.
Shamim had a Kamil degree from a madrasa and held bachelor's and master's degrees from Jagannath University. He had also authored a religious book titled 'Antordrishti'.

An analysis of 33 Facebook posts by The Daily Star found that the online campaign dehumanized Shamim and celebrated his death. Nearly three-quarters of the comments on one of the posts celebrating the killing were supportive of the violence.
caption:
A private audio clip and viral Facebook posts led to the [[mob killing of a young man]] in Satkhira. He was a madrasa and university graduate who had written a religious book.

Wahiduzzaman Shamim was beaten to death by a mob in Satkhira's Debhata after being accused of making derogatory remarks about Islam. The violence escalated following viral Facebook posts and live broadcasts that identified him and incited a crowd.

An audio recording of a private conversation between Shamim and his wife, recorded during an argument, went viral on October 12. This recording sparked tension and led to allegations that he had insulted religion.

On October 13, a local religious speaker, Fazlul Haque Ameni, went live on Facebook twice, naming Shamim and demanding his punishment. This was followed by a procession of over 200 people who dragged Shamim out of a health complex and beat him again.

Despite attempts by police and medical staff to stop the attackers, Shamim died before reaching Satkhira Medical College Hospital. He leaves behind two children, aged eight years and seven months.

Shamim had a Kamil degree from a madrasa and held bachelor's and master's degrees from Jagannath University. He had also authored a religious book titled 'Antordrishti'.

An analysis of 33 Facebook posts by The Daily Star found that the online campaign dehumanized Shamim and celebrated his death. Nearly three-quarters of the comments on one of the posts celebrating the killing were supportive of the violence.
